correctness.rationale: Weighted Lq duality gives Δ^r=Σ_j p_j|N_j/(np_j)−1|^r, finite a.s. For 1<r<2, finite-dimensional multinomial CLT with tail bound Σ_{j>J}p_j^{1−r/2} proves Gaussian weighted ℓ^r limit after sqrt(n). At r=2 the large-intensity core Pearson statistic has expectation J+O(1) and variance O(J) via a degenerate two-sample kernel, while O(sqrt(log n)) fringe and no-rare-hit tail are negligible; nΔ²/log n→1/|logρ| in probability. For r>2, moving indices K_n+k converge to independent Poisson(τρ^k), and high-intensity centered-binomial moment and rare-hit low-intensity bounds make both bi-infinite tails tight, proving the log-lattice subsequential limit. Tonelli gives EΔ^r=∞ for r≥2 at every n. Finite checker assertions do not prove these weak limits.
